summary:
Red team of part 1 of the Galois representations and modularity area: seven roadmaps and 58 stages (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison 15, AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII 10, IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration 8, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations 7, IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants 7, PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure 6, TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure 5). They were read with the integrated decompositions of the two Galois-representation roadmaps, against parts 2 and 3 and the whole atlas. There are 35 findings: 9 high, 18 medium and 8 low.

The nine high findings:
(1) ET.6 follows Scholze's proof of local Langlands, which needs cyclic base change, unitary-to-GL_n base change and automorphic induction; the atlas plans these only in ET.7a, after ET.6.
(2) The Fujiwara–Varshavsky trace formula is planned only in ET.5, but ET.6's global step needs it earlier.
(3) AG2.1b's Shin route needs Mantovan's product formula and the Harris–Taylor computation of Mant_{b,μ}, which nothing plans.
(4) AG2.1b and ET.5 import Igusa varieties from IG.0–IG.1, which cover only the split noncompact datum, while Shin needs his compact datum with p possibly ramified.
(5) Nothing plans the Langlands–Kottwitz description of isogeny classes: Kottwitz point counting, Tate's isogeny theorem over finite fields, and Honda–Tate.
(6) R01.3 owns Ogg's formula with no inputs, and its residue-characteristic-2 case needs Saito's theorem.
(7) No layer states the automorphy lifting theorems over CM fields; PA.1, PA.2 and PA.4 have no consumers.
(8) The accepted RS-14 sends Hilbert-modular Igusa needs to IG.1, which cannot supply them.
(9) Scholze's torsion Galois-determinant theorem (Thm 5.4.1) has no owner, although IG.6 and PA need it.

The medium findings fall into three groups:
- Missing owners or inputs: Kottwitz's Tamagawa formula, class-field-theory inputs for ET.0, Harish-Chandra character theory, deformation rings for PA.3, the toroidal Hodge–Tate map for IG.3, congruence modules, and Brauer–Nesbitt for R01.1.
- Out-of-date targets: ET.5 calls the twisted fundamental lemma unproved; AG2.6 ignores arXiv 2607.11763 (July 2026), which gives local–global compatibility at p over CM fields; ET.1 omits Kottwitz–Shelstad's 2012 sign correction.
- Duplicates: Bun_G and the affine Grassmannian in ET.2b and GlobalShtukas; Taylor–Wiles primes in PA.4 and G7; determinant laws in R19.6 and AG2.4 against IHG; GSp₄ Galois representations; and the compatible-system carrier.

The low findings are spurious gaps in two integrated nodes, missing Chebotarev edges and presentation points. The coordinator extracted or reviewed 43 of the papers mentioning these roadmaps and reviewed the EXT-12 packets; neither is covered here.

findings.claim: ET.6 follows Scholze's LLC proof (§§2–14), which needs three automorphic inputs that no stage upstream of ET.6 plans: (a) Arthur–Clozel local cyclic base change for GL_n (existence and uniqueness of lifts, decomposition of non-supercuspidal lifts) in §12, used to prove bijectivity; (b) Clozel's base change from the auxiliary unitary group to GL_n, in the Harris–Taylor §VI form, in §10; (c) automorphic induction, Harris's non-Galois automorphic induction and Henniart's highly-ramified twisting in §§13–14, used to prove L/ε compatibility. The only stage that plans Arthur–Clozel base change or automorphic induction is ET.7a, and ET.7a requires ET.6, so it cannot supply them. No ancestor of ET.6 in data/atlas.json mentions Arthur–Clozel. ET.6's own text plans none of these steps. ET.4, ET.6's only trace-formula input, is written for CSnc's groups G_(n_i) and the simple stable-elliptic identity, not for the Harris–Taylor unitary group or local lifting of representations. As planned, ET.6's bijectivity and L/ε compatibility, the parts that make it 'the standard correspondence', have no supplier.

findings.claim: Scholze's main theorem is owned by no layer. It gives continuous n-dimensional determinants valued in the Hecke algebra of H^i(X_K, Z/p^m) for GL_n over a totally real or CM field, modulo a nilpotent ideal of bounded exponent: Theorem 5.3.1 for interior cohomology, and Theorem 5.4.1 for full cohomology by induction over the GL_n Borel–Serre boundary. TC disclaims it, IHG.5 is only a schema, and CC.8 assigns 'torsion Galois determinants' to IHG. Yet IG.6 consumes 'lower-rank torsion Galois systems' as supplied by TC and IHG, and PA's patching 'retains nilpotent error ideals'. The GL_n boundary induction is also unplanned, because TC.3 treats only symplectic and unitary parabolics.
findings.evidence: TC record: 'The target is a reusable library underlying its argument, not an additional requirement to formalize its final Galois-representation theorem.' TC.4: 'No new terminal claim about all Galois representations of all groups is part of this layer.' TC.3: 'For the symplectic/unitary parabolics whose Levi contains a restriction of scalars of GL_n'. IHG.5: 'Provide theorem schemas which take an actual geometric Hecke comparison ... The geometric comparison itself is built by TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure'. CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8: 'automorphic-section comparisons, torsion Galois determinants, vanishing, and Banach local–global compatibility remain respectively TC/IHG/IG/R31 theorems'. IG.6: 'Using lower-rank torsion Galois systems and actual Hecke polynomial factorization, prove the length obstruction'. IG document: 'TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure and IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants supply existing lower-rank torsion systems'. PA document: 'retains nilpotent error ideals'. Source: Scholze, Annals 182, Theorem 5.4.1, p. 1058: 'There exists an integer N = N([F:Q],n) ... Then there is an ideal I ⊂ T_{F,S}(K,ξ,i,m) with I^N = 0 such that there is an n-dimensional continuous determinant D of G_{F,S} with values in T_{F,S}(K,ξ,i,m)/I, satisfying D(1−X Frob_v) = P_v(X) for all v ∉ S'. findings.claim: ET.5 calls the general twisted fundamental lemma 'unproved', which is out of date. Waldspurger showed that the ordinary FL plus the nonstandard FL imply the twisted FL for unit elements, and Ngô proved both. Lemaire–Mœglin–Waldspurger (Ann. Sci. ENS 51, 2018) extended it to the whole spherical Hecke algebra. ET.3 is inconsistent as a result. It plans the nonstandard FL 'actually needed in Waldspurger's reduction', whose purpose is exactly that reduction to the twisted FL. Yet it states that no twisted FL is to be obtained, and no ET stage consumes the nonstandard FL for anything else.
findings.evidence: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.5: 'The ordinary Igusa stabilization route explicitly avoids an unproved general twisted fundamental lemma.' EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.3: 'Prove both the ordinary and the nonstandard variant actually needed in Waldspurger's reduction' and 'a general twisted or weighted fundamental lemma is not smuggled into the ordinary theorem'. Source: B. C. Ngô, 'Le lemme fondamental pour les algèbres de Lie', Publ. Math. IHÉS 111 (2010), https://www.numdam.org/article/PMIHES_2010__111__1_0.pdf (read 2026-09-24), §1.12: 'Cette égalité a été conjecturée par Waldspurger qui l'appelle le lemme fondamental non standard. Dans [83], il a démontré que la conjonction du lemme fondamental ordinaire 1.11.1 et du lemme non standard ci-dessus implique le lemme fondamental tordu.' Lemaire–Mœglin–Waldspurger, arXiv:1506.03383 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.03383, read 2026-09-24), abstract: 'We show here that the fundamental lemma for twisted endoscopy, now proved for the unit elements in the spherical Hecke algebras, implies the fundamental lemma for all elements of these Hecke algebras.'

findings.claim: ET.1 builds the transfer factors from Langlands–Shelstad and Kottwitz–Shelstad (1999) only. ET.0 builds twisted matching and ET.4 a twisted comparison. findings.claim: TC treats the CM/unitary arithmetic branch as unconditional and only the symplectic branch as conditional. It attributes this split to Scholze's Theorem 1.0.3, which says something different. The source makes CM fields unconditional only when F contains an imaginary quadratic field and S comes from a finite set of rational primes, via Shin's cohomological base change for unitary similitude groups. The general CM case depends on Mok's classification, conditional like Arthur's. None of these hypotheses appears in TC.
findings.evidence: TC document: 'The CM/unitary realization uses the stated ET/AG2/Shin hypotheses. The totally-real symplectic realization additionally requires Arthur's endoscopic transfer/classification input ... Scholze's published Theorem 1.0.3 already distinguishes the branches.' TC.3: 'the symplectic instance of TC.3 retains the explicitly conditional Arthur input above; only the matching CM/unitary instance consumes AG2's constructed characteristic-zero package.' No TC text mentions an imaginary quadratic subfield. Source: Scholze, Annals 182, Theorem 1.0.3, p. 948: 'Conjecture 1.0.2 holds true if F is CM and contains an imaginary-quadratic field. Assuming the work of Arthur, [3], it holds true if F is totally real or CM.' p. 1031: 'We need the existence of the associated endoscopic transfer, due to Arthur, [3] (resp. Mok, [47], in the unitary case). These results are still conditional on the stabilization of the twisted trace formula. However, in the unitary case, there are unconditional results of Shin, [57].' Note that Shin's result is stated in terms of unitary similitude groups.'

findings.claim: The node and its gap record a spurious hole in Serre's argument that irreducibility over the coefficient field implies absolute irreducibility for odd rho, and restrict it needlessly to GL_2(F_p). The 'reducible but indecomposable over F_p-bar' case cannot occur for an irreducible representation over a finite (perfect) field, and the node itself gives the one-line argument (a unique stable line is Galois-stable, hence rational); Serre's eigenvalue argument uses only that +1 and -1 are distinct in odd characteristic, so it works over every finite field, as the stage requires.
findings.evidence: Node statement: 'As printed the argument treats only a decomposition into a direct sum; the case of a reducible but indecomposable rho over F_p-bar (unique stable line, hence Galois-stable and rational) is not addressed in the passage.' Hypothesis: 'the oddness-to-absolute-irreducibility argument needs p different from 2 ... and rho with values in GL_2(F_p)'. Gap: 'The stage R01.4 asks for this implication in general; a complete argument must be supplied or sourced.' Stage R01.4: 'an odd, irreducible two-dimensional representation over a finite field is absolutely irreducible'. Source quoted in the node (Serre, Duke 54 (1987), 3.3, p. 198): 'det rho est impair, donc ... les valeurs propres de rho(c) sont +1 et -1; du fait que p != 2, ces valeurs propres sont distinctes'.
findings.fix: Replace the gap by a proof node: over a finite field k of odd characteristic, if rho is k-irreducible and rho tensor k-bar has a stable line, either the line is unique (then it is Gal(k-bar/k)-stable and descends, contradiction) or rho tensor k-bar splits as two lines, which must be the eigenlines of rho(c) for the distinct eigenvalues +1, -1 in F_p, hence k-rational; drop the GL_2(F_p) restriction.

findings.claim: The node records as unbridged the passage from Chenevier's Theorem B (algebraically closed residue field) to Hecke algebras with finite residue field.
